questions.stem: Values may be defined as
options: the amount of money a person earns
laws made by the National Assembly
the beliefs and standards that guide the behaviour of people in a society
the prices of goods in the market
questions.explanation: Values are the ideals and principles that a society holds as important and which guide conduct.

questions.stem: A person who consistently tells the truth and does not cheat is said to be
questions.explanation: Honesty means being truthful, sincere and free from deceit.

questions.stem: Chiamaka found a wallet containing ₦50,000 in the school library and handed it to the principal. The value she displayed is
questions.explanation: Integrity is doing what is right and upright even when no one is watching.

questions.stem: Being satisfied with what one has legitimately acquired is known as
questions.explanation: Contentment is satisfaction with one's lawful possessions; it guards against corruption and greed.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of lack of contentment in society?
questions.explanation: Discontent and greed push people into corruption, fraud and other illegal means of acquiring wealth.

questions.stem: Respect for all forms of honest work, no matter how lowly, is described as
questions.explanation: Dignity of labour means every lawful job is honourable.

questions.stem: The ability to do what is right in the face of danger or opposition is
questions.explanation: Courage is moral or physical bravery in the face of fear, danger or criticism.

questions.stem: Which of the following best demonstrates the value of cooperation?
options: A trader hoarding goods to raise prices
A driver refusing to give way to an ambulance
Community members working together to clear a blocked drainage
questions.explanation: Cooperation is working together towards a common goal.

questions.stem: Self-reliance as a value is best shown by a youth who
options: depends on relatives for all needs
joins a gang to make quick money
learns a trade and starts a small business instead of waiting for government employment
spends all day on social media
questions.explanation: Self-reliance is the ability to depend on one's own skills and efforts for survival.

questions.stem: Tolerance as a civic value means
options: accepting and respecting people whose opinions, religion or culture differ from yours
refusing to listen to other people
punishing those who disagree with you
questions.explanation: Tolerance promotes peaceful coexistence in a diverse country like Nigeria.

questions.stem: Which of the following agencies is mainly responsible for promoting national values and enlightenment among Nigerians?
questions.explanation: The NOA is charged with public enlightenment and promoting positive values and attitudes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a moral value?
questions.explanation: Moral values are standards of right conduct such as honesty, fairness and integrity.

questions.stem: Discipline as a value is best described as
options: the use of punishment on others
the ability to control oneself and act according to rules
questions.explanation: Self-discipline is self-control and orderly conduct in line with rules and norms.

questions.stem: A public officer who refuses a bribe offered by a contractor even though nobody would find out displays
questions.explanation: Integrity is consistent adherence to moral principles regardless of opportunity or observation.

questions.stem: Citizenship education helps students mainly to
options: know their rights and duties as members of the state
questions.explanation: Civic and citizenship education produces informed, responsible citizens.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty of a good citizen?
options: Obeying the laws of the country
questions.explanation: Duties include obeying laws, paying taxes, voting and protecting public property.

questions.stem: Nationalism can be defined as
options: loyalty to one's ethnic group above the nation
strong love for and loyalty to one's nation and its interests
the act of travelling across many nations
questions.explanation: Nationalism is devotion to the nation, including the desire for its unity, independence and progress.

questions.stem: The green colour in the Nigerian national flag represents
questions.explanation: Green stands for agriculture (the land's fertility) and white for peace and unity.

questions.stem: The eagle on the Nigerian coat of arms symbolises
questions.explanation: The eagle represents strength; the black shield stands for fertile soil.

questions.stem: The wavy white Y-shaped band on the shield of the Nigerian coat of arms represents
questions.explanation: The Y depicts the confluence of the Niger and Benue rivers at Lokoja.

questions.stem: The motto of the Federal Republic of Nigeria is
options: Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress
questions.explanation: The national motto on the coat of arms is 'Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress'.

questions.stem: Since 2024, Nigeria's official national anthem has been
questions.explanation: The National Anthem Act of 2024 restored 'Nigeria, We Hail Thee', the independence anthem, replacing 'Arise, O Compatriots'.

questions.stem: Which of the following can promote national unity in Nigeria?
options: The National Youth Service Corps scheme
questions.explanation: NYSC posts graduates to states other than their own, encouraging understanding among ethnic groups.

questions.stem: The National Youth Service Corps was established in
questions.explanation: The NYSC was set up in 1973 to promote national unity after the civil war.

questions.stem: A citizen who places the interests of his ethnic group above those of the nation in public appointments is guilty of
questions.explanation: Tribalism undermines national unity; patriotism and nationalism put the nation first.

questions.stem: Patriotism is best demonstrated by a citizen who
options: buys only foreign goods to show off
reports a plan to vandalise an oil pipeline to the security agencies
speaks badly of the country abroad
questions.explanation: Patriotism means love of country shown through actions that protect and advance it.

questions.stem: Human rights are
options: the basic rights and freedoms that belong to every person
rights enjoyed only by rich people
questions.explanation: Human rights are inherent, universal and inalienable entitlements of all human beings.

questions.stem: The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted by the United Nations General Assembly in
questions.explanation: It was adopted on 10 December 1948, now celebrated as Human Rights Day.

questions.stem: Human Rights Day is observed every year on
questions.explanation: 10 December marks the adoption of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 1948.

questions.stem: The African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights is also known as the
questions.explanation: Adopted in 1981, it is called the Banjul Charter after the Gambian capital where it was drafted.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a civil and political right?
questions.explanation: Civil and political rights include life, expression, assembly, fair hearing and voting.

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution, a person arrested for an offence must be informed of the reasons in writing within
options: 24 hours, in a language he understands
questions.explanation: Section 35(3) requires that an arrested person be informed in writing within 24 hours of the facts and grounds of arrest, in a language he understands.

questions.stem: Which of the following rights is restricted when a convicted person is sentenced to imprisonment?
options: Right to dignity of the human person
Right to be recognised as a person
questions.explanation: Section 35 permits deprivation of liberty in execution of a court sentence; dignity and freedom from torture remain.

questions.stem: The body set up in Nigeria in 1995 to promote and protect human rights is the
questions.explanation: The NHRC monitors, investigates and promotes human rights.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of human rights abuse?
options: Torturing a suspect to obtain a confession
Giving a suspect access to a lawyer
Charging a suspect to court promptly
questions.explanation: Torture violates the right to dignity of the human person (section 34).

questions.stem: The Child's Rights Act was passed by the National Assembly in
questions.explanation: The Child's Rights Act of 2003 domesticates the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child; states must adopt it.

questions.stem: Which of the following agencies protects the rights of citizens against abuse by public officers by receiving and investigating complaints?
questions.explanation: The Public Complaints Commission acts as Nigeria's ombudsman.

questions.stem: A major limitation to the enjoyment of human rights in Nigeria is
options: the provisions of Chapter IV of the constitution
illiteracy and ignorance of rights by many citizens
the activities of human rights groups
questions.explanation: Many people do not know their rights or cannot afford to seek redress, limiting enforcement.

questions.stem: Freedom of association guaranteed in the 1999 Constitution allows a citizen to
options: form or belong to a trade union or political party
take the law into his own hands
questions.explanation: Section 40 protects assembly and association, but secret societies are excluded by section 38(4).

questions.stem: Law may be defined as
options: a set of moral advice by parents
the customs of a single family
a body of rules made by a recognised authority and enforced by the state
questions.explanation: Laws are binding rules backed by state sanctions.

questions.stem: Which of the following agencies is mainly responsible for maintaining law and order in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The police prevent and detect crime and maintain public order.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of lawlessness in a society?
questions.explanation: Breakdown of law and order leads to insecurity, which drives away investment.

questions.stem: Jungle justice refers to
options: a judgement delivered by the Supreme Court
a trial in a customary court
the punishment of suspected offenders by a mob without trial
the use of forests as prisons
questions.explanation: Mob justice denies suspects the right to fair hearing and may punish innocent people.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way of promoting law and order in schools?
options: Clear rules and fair enforcement of discipline
Allowing students to settle disputes by fighting
questions.explanation: Clear, fairly enforced rules encourage orderly behaviour.

questions.stem: Bola saw a man stealing a motorcycle. The most appropriate civic action for him is to
options: report the incident to the nearest police station
gather a mob to beat the thief
keep quiet because it is not his business
questions.explanation: Citizens should report crimes and allow law enforcement and courts to act.

questions.stem: Which of the following courts has the power to try cases involving Islamic personal law at the highest level in a state?
questions.explanation: States that wish may establish a Sharia Court of Appeal for Islamic personal law matters.

questions.stem: A rule of conduct accepted by a society through long practice is called
questions.explanation: Customs are traditional practices that guide behaviour and may become customary law.

questions.stem: The Nigerian Correctional Service, which manages custodial centres, was formerly known as the
options: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.explanation: The Nigerian Correctional Service Act of 2019 renamed the Prisons Service and emphasised reformation.

questions.stem: Responsible parenthood means
options: having as many children as possible
parents providing adequately for the physical, emotional and moral needs of their children
sending all children to boarding school
questions.explanation: Responsible parents care for, guide, educate and protect their children.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty of responsible parents?
options: Using children as street hawkers during school hours
Encouraging children to drop out of school
questions.explanation: Parents must educate, feed, clothe, protect and morally guide their children.

questions.stem: Child abuse includes
options: subjecting a child to hard labour that endangers his health
praising a child for good conduct
taking a sick child to hospital
questions.explanation: Child labour, neglect, physical, sexual and emotional maltreatment are forms of abuse.

questions.stem: Family planning helps parents to
options: have the number of children they can adequately cater for
questions.explanation: Spacing and limiting births lets parents meet children's needs.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of irresponsible parenthood?
questions.explanation: Neglected children are more likely to become delinquents, drop-outs or street children.

questions.stem: Mr and Mrs Okafor spend time with their children each evening, check their homework and discuss values. This mainly helps to
options: build strong family bonds and good character in the children
replace the role of teachers entirely
questions.explanation: Parental involvement and communication promote character, discipline and performance.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of responsible parenthood?
options: Shielding a child from punishment for every wrongdoing
questions.explanation: Over-protection from correction encourages indiscipline; responsible parents guide and correct with love.

questions.stem: Traffic regulations are
options: rules guiding the use of roads by motorists, cyclists and pedestrians
questions.explanation: They promote safety and orderly movement on the road.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for road safety administration on Nigerian highways is the
questions.explanation: The FRSC, established in 1988, manages road safety on highways.

questions.stem: At a traffic light, the red signal means
questions.explanation: Red means stop, amber (yellow) means get ready or prepare to stop, green means go when safe.

questions.stem: Pedestrians should cross the road at
options: a zebra crossing or pedestrian bridge
questions.explanation: Zebra crossings and footbridges are designated safe crossing points.

questions.stem: Triangular road signs generally
options: warn road users of danger ahead
questions.explanation: Triangular signs warn; circular signs give orders; rectangular signs give information.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a traffic offence?
options: Using a mobile phone while driving
questions.explanation: Phone use while driving distracts the driver and is prohibited.

questions.stem: The main reason why drivers should not drink alcohol before driving is that alcohol
options: makes the car consume more fuel
slows reaction time and impairs judgement
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects coordination and judgement, causing crashes.

questions.stem: Kunle, a commercial motorcyclist, carries three passengers at once without helmets. He is guilty of
options: overloading and failing to provide crash helmets
questions.explanation: Overloading and riding without helmets endanger lives and violate traffic rules.

questions.stem: An octagonal (eight-sided) red road sign means
questions.explanation: The red octagon is reserved for the STOP sign so it is recognisable even from its shape.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of road accidents in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Over-speeding, bad roads, drunk driving, poor maintenance and fatigue cause many crashes.

questions.stem: A circular road sign with a red border generally
questions.explanation: Red-bordered circles are prohibitory signs, for example no entry or no U-turn.

questions.stem: Inter-personal relationship refers to
options: the association or interaction between two or more people
the link between a person and his property
the relationship between plants and animals
questions.explanation: It covers relations among family, friends, classmates, colleagues and neighbours.

questions.stem: Which of the following promotes good inter-personal relationships?
questions.explanation: Clear, respectful communication builds trust and understanding.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a type of inter-personal relationship?
questions.explanation: Friendship, marriage, family, work and neighbourly relations are types.

questions.stem: Dialogue as a skill in resolving conflict means
options: one party forcing its will on the other
taking the matter straight to violence
parties discussing their differences to reach understanding
questions.explanation: Dialogue involves listening and talking to reach agreement.

questions.stem: Which of the following can damage inter-personal relationships?
questions.explanation: Lies and deceit destroy trust, which is the foundation of relationships.

questions.stem: Empathy in relationships means
options: the ability to understand and share another person's feelings
questions.explanation: Empathy is putting oneself in another's position and understanding their feelings.

questions.stem: Two classmates, Aisha and Ngozi, quarrel over a borrowed textbook. The best way to settle the matter is by
options: reporting to their parents' religious leaders only
discussing calmly, with a neutral person mediating if needed
refusing to speak to each other forever
questions.explanation: Mediation and negotiation are peaceful conflict-resolution methods.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a benefit of good inter-personal relationships?
questions.explanation: Good relationships promote harmony, cooperation and support.

questions.stem: A cult is
options: a group whose members share secret beliefs and practices, often hidden from the public
questions.explanation: Secret cults conceal membership and activities and are often associated with violence.

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution, the right to freedom of association does NOT include the right to
options: be a member of a secret society
questions.explanation: Section 38(4) states that nothing entitles any person to form, take part in or be a member of a secret society.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of cultism in tertiary institutions?
options: Peer pressure and the quest for protection
questions.explanation: Peer influence, desire for power or protection, poor parenting and moral decay draw students into cults.

questions.stem: A consequence of cultism in schools is
options: violence leading to loss of lives and disruption of academic programmes
questions.explanation: Cult clashes cause deaths, injuries and closure of institutions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way to curb cultism in schools?
options: Expelling and prosecuting cult members and enlightening students
questions.explanation: Firm sanctions, orientation, counselling and wholesome extracurricular activities help reduce cultism.

questions.stem: A student who is being pressured to join a cult should first
options: refuse firmly and report to a trusted teacher, counsellor or parent
stop attending school without telling anyone
questions.explanation: Reporting allows adults and authorities to protect the student and act against the cult.

questions.stem: Which of the following signs may suggest that a student has joined a secret cult?
options: Sudden secrecy, unexplained injuries and association with violent groups
questions.explanation: Sudden change of behaviour, secrecy, scars and new violent associates are common warning signs.

questions.stem: The cult activities that have spread to some secondary schools and communities in Nigeria are dangerous mainly because they
options: expose young people to crime, drugs and violence
questions.explanation: Cultism drags youths into criminality, drug abuse and violent clashes.

questions.stem: Drug abuse means
options: the use of drugs prescribed by a doctor
the use of drugs in a way or amount not prescribed or approved by a qualified health worker
the sale of drugs in a pharmacy
the storage of drugs in a cool place
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is the non-medical or excessive use of substances, leading to harm.

questions.stem: The agency responsible for fighting illicit drug trafficking in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The NDLEA, established in 1989, enforces laws against illicit drugs.

questions.stem: The agency that regulates the manufacture, importation and sale of food and drugs in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control regulates drugs, food and related products.

questions.stem: Which of the following is classified as a stimulant?
questions.explanation: Cocaine stimulates the central nervous system; alcohol, heroin and Valium are depressants.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a common sign of drug abuse in a student?
options: Sudden decline in academic performance and withdrawal from friends
questions.explanation: Behavioural change, poor grades, red eyes and isolation are common signs.

questions.stem: The illicit drug most widely abused in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: National surveys show cannabis is the most commonly used illicit drug in Nigeria.

questions.stem: Excessive use of codeine-containing cough syrup by youths is dangerous mainly because it
options: can cause addiction and damage to vital organs
has no side effects at all
questions.explanation: Codeine is an opioid; misuse causes dependence, organ damage and mental health problems.

questions.stem: International Day against Drug Abuse and Illicit Trafficking is observed every year on
questions.explanation: The UN marks 26 June to raise awareness of drug abuse.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of drug abuse?
questions.explanation: Drug abuse can cause psychosis, addiction, crime and death.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way of preventing drug abuse among youths?
options: Public enlightenment on the dangers of drugs
questions.explanation: Education, counselling, parental guidance and law enforcement help prevent abuse.

questions.stem: Peer pressure contributes to drug abuse mainly because young people
options: want to be accepted by their friends
are forced by law to take drugs
are paid by NAFDAC to try drugs
learn about drugs only from textbooks
questions.explanation: The desire to belong makes adolescents copy friends' behaviour, including drug use.

questions.stem: Human trafficking is
options: the legal movement of workers with valid visas
the recruitment, transport or harbouring of persons by force or deception for exploitation
the transport of goods across borders
questions.explanation: Trafficking involves an act (recruitment, transport), a means (force, fraud, deception) and a purpose (exploitation).

questions.stem: The Nigerian agency responsible for fighting human trafficking is
questions.explanation: The National Agency for the Prohibition of Trafficking in Persons was established in 2003.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of human trafficking?
questions.explanation: Poverty, unemployment, ignorance and greed make people vulnerable to traffickers' false promises.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of human trafficking?
questions.explanation: Forms include forced labour, sexual exploitation, domestic servitude, child soldiering and organ harvesting.

questions.stem: Traffickers often lure victims by
options: telling them the truth about their work
giving them valid travel documents in their own names
involving the police in the arrangement
questions.explanation: Deceptive job offers are a common recruitment method.

questions.stem: Amaka is offered a 'free' trip to Europe to work as a hairdresser, but she must swear an oath of secrecy and repay a huge debt on arrival. This is most likely
questions.explanation: Debt bondage, secrecy oaths and vague job offers are classic signs of trafficking.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of human trafficking for victims?
options: Exposure to sexually transmitted infections and psychological trauma
questions.explanation: Victims suffer abuse, disease, trauma, loss of freedom and sometimes death.

questions.stem: A way of reducing human trafficking is
options: creating job opportunities and enlightening people on its dangers
questions.explanation: Economic empowerment, awareness campaigns and prosecution reduce trafficking.

questions.stem: Child trafficking is often aimed at
options: using children as domestic servants or street hawkers
questions.explanation: Trafficked children are exploited for labour, begging or sex.

questions.stem: HIV stands for
questions.explanation: HIV is the virus that weakens the immune system and can lead to AIDS.

questions.stem: AIDS stands for
questions.explanation: AIDS is the advanced stage of HIV infection.

questions.stem: HIV can be transmitted through
options: sharing unsterilised sharp objects such as needles and razors
questions.explanation: HIV spreads through blood, sexual fluids, and from mother to child; not through casual contact or insects.

questions.stem: HIV mainly attacks the body's
questions.explanation: HIV destroys CD4 white blood cells, weakening immunity.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a way HIV is transmitted?
options: Unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
From an infected mother to her child
questions.explanation: HIV is not transmitted by hugging, sharing toilets or eating together.

questions.stem: Drugs used to suppress HIV in the body are known as
questions.explanation: Antiretroviral therapy reduces viral load and allows people with HIV to live long, healthy lives; it is not a cure.

questions.stem: World AIDS Day is observed annually on
questions.explanation: World AIDS Day on 1 December raises awareness and remembers those who died.

questions.stem: Stigmatisation of people living with HIV is harmful mainly because it
options: discourages people from testing and seeking treatment
questions.explanation: Fear of discrimination stops people knowing their status and accessing care, which spreads infection.

questions.stem: The only sure way to know whether a person is infected with HIV is
options: by looking at the person's body weight
questions.explanation: Many people with HIV look healthy for years; only testing confirms status.

questions.stem: Which of the following reduces the risk of mother-to-child transmission of HIV?
options: Antiretroviral treatment for the mother during pregnancy and breastfeeding
questions.explanation: PMTCT programmes use antiretrovirals and safe delivery and feeding practices.

questions.stem: Youth empowerment means
options: giving youths money to spend freely
equipping young people with skills, knowledge and resources to become self-reliant
questions.explanation: Empowerment builds capacity, skills and opportunities for young people.

questions.stem: Which of the following agencies was established in 1986 to tackle unemployment in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The NDE runs vocational training, small business and rural employment schemes.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a youth empowerment skill?
questions.explanation: Vocational skills like tailoring, ICT, welding and catering enable self-employment.

questions.stem: The agency that supports small and medium enterprises in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The Small and Medium Enterprises Development Agency of Nigeria promotes small businesses.

questions.stem: A benefit of youth empowerment to the nation is
questions.explanation: Empowered youths are productive and less likely to engage in crime.

questions.stem: A major obstacle to youth empowerment programmes in Nigeria is
options: poor funding and lack of continuity of programmes
questions.explanation: Programmes often suffer from inadequate funds, corruption and abandonment.

questions.stem: Emeka, an NCE graduate, took a short course in solar panel installation and now employs two apprentices. This illustrates
questions.explanation: Acquiring practical skills enables graduates to create jobs rather than seek them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why youths should be empowered?
options: To make them dependent on politicians
To keep them at home permanently
To make them productive and self-reliant
questions.explanation: Empowerment helps youths contribute to national development.

questions.stem: The three tiers of government in Nigeria are
questions.explanation: The tiers are levels of government; the arms are executive, legislature and judiciary.

questions.stem: The arm of government that implements laws is the
questions.explanation: The executive carries out laws and runs the administration.

questions.stem: The law-making body of a state in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: Each state has a unicameral House of Assembly.

questions.stem: The chief executive of a state in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: The Governor heads the state executive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of the judiciary?
questions.explanation: Courts interpret laws, settle disputes and protect rights.

questions.stem: The President of Nigeria holds office for a term of
questions.explanation: Under the 1999 Constitution, the President may serve at most two four-year terms.

questions.stem: Under the Not Too Young To Run amendment of 2018, the minimum age to contest for the office of President in Nigeria is
questions.explanation: The 2018 amendment reduced the presidential age qualification from 40 to 35.

questions.stem: Under the 1999 Constitution as amended, the minimum age to contest for a seat in the House of Representatives is
questions.explanation: The Not Too Young To Run amendment reduced it from 30 to 25 years.

questions.stem: The Federal Executive Council in Nigeria is made up of the President, the Vice-President and
options: the Ministers of the Government of the Federation
the Justices of the Supreme Court
questions.explanation: The FEC is the President's cabinet; the constitution requires at least one Minister from each state.

questions.stem: The head of a local government council in Nigeria is the
questions.explanation: An elected chairman heads the local government executive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of government?
questions.explanation: Government protects life and property, provides services and maintains order.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Democracy is a system of government in which
options: power belongs to the people who exercise it directly or through elected representatives
a king rules by divine right
questions.explanation: Democracy rests on popular sovereignty and periodic elections.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Nigeria celebrates Democracy Day on
questions.explanation: Since 2019 Democracy Day has been observed on 12 June in recognition of the 1993 election.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a pillar of democracy?
questions.explanation: Pillars include independent courts, free press, rule of law, free elections and respect for rights.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: The rule of law requires that
options: only the poor obey the law
everybody, including government officials, is subject to the law
questions.explanation: Supremacy of law and equality before it are core elements.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: National development refers to
options: an increase in the population only
the growth of one ethnic group
sustained improvement in the economic, social and political life of a nation
questions.explanation: Development covers growth in income, welfare, infrastructure, education and institutions.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following hinders national development?
questions.explanation: Corruption diverts resources from public projects and erodes trust.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: How does respect for the rule of law contribute to national development?
options: It creates a stable environment that attracts investment
questions.explanation: Predictable laws and secure property rights encourage investors and economic growth.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Direct democracy is practicable mainly in
options: small communities where all citizens can meet to decide
questions.explanation: Direct democracy, like that of ancient Athens, needs a small population.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of democracy?
questions.explanation: Regular free elections let citizens choose and change leaders.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following shows respect for the rule of law?
options: A government obeying a court judgement against it
questions.explanation: Compliance with court orders demonstrates that government is under the law.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following best explains why free press is important for democracy?
options: It informs citizens and exposes abuses of power
It writes the laws of the country
questions.explanation: A free press enables informed choices and accountability.

questions.stem: Political apathy means
options: lack of interest in political activities
questions.explanation: Apathy is indifference to politics, shown in low voting and participation.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a cause of political apathy?
questions.explanation: When votes seem not to count or elections are violent, citizens withdraw.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a consequence of political apathy?
questions.explanation: If good citizens stay away, the unfit can easily win power.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way of reducing political apathy?
options: Political education and conduct of credible elections
questions.explanation: Voter education, credible elections and accountable leadership encourage participation.

questions.stem: Tunde, a 22-year-old, says 'My vote will not count anyway', and does not collect his voter's card. His attitude is an example of
questions.explanation: Refusing to participate out of disillusionment is apathy.

questions.stem: A low turnout of voters at an election is a sign of
questions.explanation: Low turnout reflects disinterest or disillusionment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is likely to discourage women from participating in politics in Nigeria?
options: Cultural and religious restrictions and the high cost of contesting
questions.explanation: Cultural barriers, violence and money politics discourage women's participation.

questions.stem: Civil society refers to
options: voluntary organisations outside government that work for the interest of citizens
questions.explanation: CSOs include NGOs, professional associations, labour unions and faith-based groups.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a civil society organisation in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Labour unions, professional bodies and NGOs are part of civil society.

questions.stem: Popular participation means
options: the involvement of only politicians in government
the active involvement of citizens in the governance of their society
the use of force to change government
questions.explanation: It includes voting, debating, petitioning, campaigning and joining associations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a function of civil society organisations?
questions.explanation: CSOs monitor governance, educate citizens and advocate for reforms.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a challenge facing civil society organisations in Nigeria?
options: Lack of any issues to address
questions.explanation: CSOs face funding problems, internal divisions and sometimes repression.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a form of popular participation?
questions.explanation: Town halls, voting and peaceful advocacy are forms of participation.

questions.stem: A coalition of NGOs in Kaduna organises public hearings on the state budget and publishes its findings. This shows that civil society
options: replaces the State House of Assembly
promotes transparency and accountability in government
questions.explanation: Budget tracking and advocacy help hold government accountable.

questions.stem: The public service is made up of
options: all persons employed by government in its ministries, agencies and parastatals
only members of the armed forces
questions.explanation: The public service includes the civil service and staff of government agencies and corporations.

questions.stem: The body that requires public officers in Nigeria to declare their assets is the
questions.explanation: The Code of Conduct Bureau receives asset declarations; the Code of Conduct Tribunal tries breaches.

questions.stem: Which of the following agencies fights corruption in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: The EFCC and ICPC investigate and prosecute corruption and financial crimes.

questions.stem: The Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC) was established in
questions.explanation: The ICPC was set up under the Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Act 2000.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a feature of a good public service in a democracy?
questions.explanation: Good public service is accountable, transparent, efficient and neutral.

questions.stem: The Freedom of Information Act, 2011 promotes good public service by
options: allowing civil servants to join parties
giving citizens the right to access public records and information
questions.explanation: Access to information enhances transparency and accountability.

questions.stem: A civil servant who uses her office to award contracts to her relatives is guilty of
questions.explanation: Nepotism is favouring relatives in appointments or contracts, a form of corruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a problem of the public service in Nigeria?
questions.explanation: Corruption, red tape, lateness and poor motivation weaken the public service.

questions.stem: The role of the public service in a democracy is to
options: implement government policies and deliver services to citizens
questions.explanation: Public servants execute policies and provide public services.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a basic need that responsible parents must provide for their children?
questions.explanation: Basic needs are food, shelter, clothing, health care and education.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why some parents fail to perform their responsibilities?
options: Poverty and having more children than they can care for
questions.explanation: Poverty and large families stretch parents' resources and attention.

questions.stem: Parents act as the first agents of socialization because they
options: teach children language, values and behaviour from birth
questions.explanation: The family is the earliest and most influential agent of socialization.

questions.stem: Giving children immunisation against childhood diseases is an aspect of
questions.explanation: Protecting children's health through immunisation is a parental duty.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a sanction imposed by a court for breaking the law?
questions.explanation: Courts may impose fines, imprisonment, community service and other penalties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an agency of law enforcement in Nigeria?
options: Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps
questions.explanation: The NSCDC, police and others enforce laws; the legislature makes them.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a reason why citizens obey laws?
options: Because laws are always written in English
To avoid sanctions and to live in peace with others
Because laws are made by foreigners
questions.explanation: People obey laws from respect for authority, fear of punishment and the desire for order.

questions.stem: Mrs Danjuma, a trader, was arrested on Friday evening. Under the 1999 Constitution, if no court of competent jurisdiction is within 40 kilometres, she must be brought before a court within
questions.explanation: Section 35(5) defines a reasonable time as one day where a court is within 40 km, otherwise two days or longer as the court considers reasonable.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a quality of a good friend?
questions.explanation: Good friends are trustworthy, loyal, honest and supportive.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a skill for maintaining good inter-personal relationships?
questions.explanation: Active listening shows respect and helps understanding.

questions.stem: When two people agree to give up part of their demands in order to settle a dispute, they have used
questions.explanation: Compromise means each side concedes something to reach agreement.

questions.stem: Which of the following statements about conflict in relationships is correct?
options: Conflict can always be avoided completely
Conflict is natural, but it should be managed constructively
Conflict should always be settled by force
questions.explanation: Disagreements are normal; what matters is resolving them peacefully.

questions.stem: Cult activities in schools are mostly carried out
questions.explanation: Cults operate secretly to avoid detection.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a role of parents in curbing cultism?
options: Giving children unlimited money without questions
Monitoring their children's friends and activities
Encouraging children to keep secrets from them
questions.explanation: Close monitoring and open communication help parents detect and prevent cult involvement.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an indication of political apathy?
options: Refusal to register as a voter
questions.explanation: Not registering or voting are typical signs of apathy.

questions.stem: Poverty can cause political apathy because
options: the constitution bars poor people from voting
people concentrate on survival rather than political activities
questions.explanation: Economic hardship makes politics seem irrelevant or out of reach.

questions.stem: Which of the following can make citizens lose confidence in the electoral process?
questions.explanation: When results are manipulated, people feel their votes are useless.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a non-governmental organisation (NGO)?
options: A registered charity that runs free health clinics
questions.explanation: NGOs are private, non-profit bodies independent of government.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a way citizens can participate in governance between elections?
questions.explanation: Petitions, public hearings and peaceful advocacy allow continuous participation.

questions.stem: Labour unions are part of civil society because they
options: are voluntary organisations that defend workers' interests independently of government
questions.explanation: Unions are member-based associations that advocate for workers.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a youth empowerment programme?
questions.explanation: Skills centres train youths in trades for self-employment.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a role of youths in national development?
options: Contributing their skills and energy to productive activities
questions.explanation: Youths are the workforce and future leaders of the nation.

questions.stem: The legislature at the federal level in Nigeria is called the
questions.explanation: The National Assembly comprises the Senate and House of Representatives.

questions.stem: Nigeria's federal capital is
questions.explanation: Abuja replaced Lagos as the capital in December 1991.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following is an index of national development?
questions.explanation: Literacy, life expectancy, income and infrastructure measure development.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem: Which of the following groups is responsible for protecting democracy in a country?
questions.explanation: Democracy depends on vigilant citizens and strong institutions.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a right of every Nigerian under the 1999 Constitution?
options: Right to own a public company
questions.explanation: Section 33 protects the right to life.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a duty that goes with the right to freedom of expression?
options: Not to join a trade union
questions.explanation: Rights carry responsibilities; free speech must not damage others' reputations by falsehood.

questions.stem: A civil servant is expected to be
questions.explanation: Civil servants serve any lawful government impartially.

questions.stem: The Code of Conduct Tribunal tries public officers who
options: breach the Code of Conduct, such as making false asset declarations
questions.explanation: The Tribunal tries breaches of the Code of Conduct for Public Officers in the Fifth Schedule.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a negative value?
questions.explanation: Greed is an undesirable trait that leads to corruption.

questions.stem: Which of the following should a motorist wear for safety while driving?
questions.explanation: Seat belts reduce injuries in crashes; motorcyclists wear helmets.

questions.stem: The amber traffic light means
options: prepare to stop or get ready
questions.explanation: Amber signals a change; drivers should prepare to stop.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a preventive measure against HIV/AIDS?
options: Abstinence from sex until marriage and faithfulness to one uninfected partner
questions.explanation: Abstinence, faithfulness, safe blood and sterile instruments prevent infection.

questions.stem: The Nigerian national pledge begins with the words
questions.explanation: The pledge is recited to express loyalty to Nigeria.

questions.stem:
(a) What are values? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four values that every Nigerian youth should possess. [8 marks]
(c) State two ways in which the school can promote good values among students. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Values are the beliefs, ideals and standards a society considers important and which guide the behaviour of its members
2 marks: Honesty: being truthful and free from deceit
2 marks: Integrity: consistently doing what is right
2 marks: Contentment: being satisfied with what one has lawfully
2 marks: Discipline, courage, tolerance, cooperation or dignity of labour (any one, explained)
2 marks: Teachers serving as good role models
2 marks: Rewarding good conduct and punishing misconduct fairly, or civic education, clubs and moral instruction
questions.explanation: Values are standards that guide conduct. Youths need honesty, integrity, contentment, discipline, courage and tolerance. Schools promote values through role models, fair rewards and sanctions, civic education and clubs.

questions.stem:
(a) Define integrity. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four consequences of lack of integrity among public officers in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) Suggest two ways of promoting integrity in public life. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles that one follows consistently, even when unobserved
2 marks: Embezzlement of public funds and corruption
2 marks: Poor infrastructure and abandoned projects
2 marks: Loss of public trust in government
2 marks: Poor international image and reduced foreign investment
2 marks: Strict enforcement of anti-corruption laws through bodies like the EFCC, ICPC and Code of Conduct Bureau
2 marks: Rewarding honest officers publicly, or value orientation through schools, religious bodies and the NOA
questions.explanation: Integrity is consistent moral uprightness. Its absence breeds corruption, abandoned projects, loss of trust and a poor image. It is promoted through enforcement of anti-corruption laws, rewarding honest officers and value education.

questions.stem:
(a) Mention three ways of acquiring Nigerian citizenship under the 1999 Constitution. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four duties of a Nigerian citizen. [8 marks]
(c) State four rights of a Nigerian citizen. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: By birth
1 mark: By registration
1 mark: By naturalisation
2 marks: Obeying the laws of the country
2 marks: Paying taxes promptly
2 marks: Voting in elections and participating in civic life
2 marks: Protecting public property, or defending the nation, or respecting the rights of others
1 mark: Right to life
1 mark: Right to freedom of expression
1 mark: Right to vote and be voted for
1 mark: Right to freedom of movement, or fair hearing, or religion
questions.explanation: Citizenship is acquired by birth, registration or naturalisation. Citizens must obey laws, pay taxes, vote and protect public property, and enjoy rights such as life, expression, voting and movement.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term nationalism. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four ways in which national symbols promote national unity in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) State two factors that hinder national unity in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Nationalism is strong love for and loyalty to one's nation, and the desire to promote its unity, independence and interests
2 marks: The national flag identifies all Nigerians as one people
2 marks: The national anthem and pledge express shared loyalty and are recited by all citizens
2 marks: The coat of arms and motto (Unity and Faith, Peace and Progress) remind citizens of common goals
2 marks: National symbols are used at national events, creating a sense of belonging beyond ethnic or religious identity
2 marks: Ethnicity and tribalism
2 marks: Religious intolerance, or corruption, or unequal distribution of resources
questions.explanation: Nationalism is devotion to the nation. The flag, anthem, pledge, coat of arms and motto foster a common identity. Unity is hindered by tribalism, religious intolerance, corruption and inequality.

questions.stem:
(a) What are human rights? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four features of human rights. [8 marks]
(c) Mention four fundamental rights guaranteed in Chapter IV of the 1999 Constitution. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Human rights are the basic rights and freedoms to which all human beings are entitled because they are human
2 marks: Universal: they apply to everyone everywhere
2 marks: Inalienable: they cannot be taken away except by due process of law
2 marks: Indivisible and interdependent: enjoyment of one right affects others
2 marks: Limited: they can be restricted in the interest of public safety, order, health or the rights of others
1 mark: Right to life
1 mark: Right to dignity of the human person
1 mark: Right to personal liberty
1 mark: Right to fair hearing, or freedom of thought, expression, movement, association or freedom from discrimination
questions.explanation: Human rights are inherent entitlements of all persons. They are universal, inalienable, indivisible and subject to lawful limits. Chapter IV guarantees life, dignity, liberty, fair hearing, expression, religion, movement, association and non-discrimination.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain four limitations to the enjoyment of human rights in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(b) Explain how each of the following protects human rights: (i) the judiciary; (ii) the National Human Rights Commission; (iii) the mass media. [6 marks]
(c) Name one international document on human rights. [1 mark]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: Illiteracy and ignorance of rights
2 marks: Poverty and the high cost of litigation
2 marks: Abuse of power by security agencies
2 marks: Delay in the administration of justice, or a declared state of emergency
2 marks: Judiciary: enforces rights through court actions, e.g. under section 46, and grants remedies
2 marks: NHRC: investigates complaints of abuse and promotes awareness
2 marks: Mass media: exposes abuses and educates the public on their rights
1 mark: Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948) or African Charter on Human and Peoples' Rights
questions.explanation: Rights are limited by ignorance, poverty, abuse by security agencies and slow justice. Courts enforce rights, the NHRC investigates and educates, and the media exposes abuses. Key documents are the UDHR and the African Charter.

questions.stem:
(a) Define law. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four reasons why citizens should obey laws. [8 marks]
(c) State two consequences of lawlessness in a society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Law is a body of rules made by a recognised authority, binding on members of society and enforced with sanctions
2 marks: To maintain peace and order
2 marks: To avoid punishment
2 marks: To protect lives and property
2 marks: To guarantee the rights and freedoms of all, or to promote development
2 marks: Insecurity, crime and loss of lives and property
2 marks: Discouragement of investment and economic decline, or anarchy
questions.explanation: Law is a body of enforceable rules. Citizens obey to keep order, avoid sanctions, protect life and property and secure rights. Lawlessness causes insecurity and economic decline.

questions.stem:
(a) What is responsible parenthood? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four roles of responsible parents in the family. [8 marks]
(c) State two consequences of irresponsible parenthood on the society. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Responsible parenthood is the ability of parents to adequately meet the physical, emotional, educational and moral needs of their children
2 marks: Providing basic needs: food, shelter, clothing and health care
2 marks: Educating children and paying school fees
2 marks: Moral and religious upbringing and being good role models
2 marks: Protecting children from abuse and harmful influences, or showing love and care
2 marks: Increase in juvenile delinquency and crime
2 marks: Increase in street children, school drop-outs or cultism
questions.explanation: Responsible parents provide for, educate, morally guide and protect their children. Irresponsible parenthood breeds delinquency, street children, drop-outs and crime.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term traffic regulations. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four causes of road accidents in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) Mention four functions of the Federal Road Safety Corps. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Traffic regulations are rules and laws guiding the use of roads by motorists, cyclists and pedestrians to ensure safety and orderly movement
2 marks: Over-speeding and reckless driving
2 marks: Driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs
2 marks: Bad roads and poor vehicle maintenance
2 marks: Use of phones while driving, fatigue, overloading or ignorance of road signs
1 mark: Preventing and minimising accidents on highways
1 mark: Clearing obstructions and giving prompt attention to accident victims
1 mark: Educating road users on road safety
1 mark: Designing and producing driver's licences and vehicle number plates, or arresting traffic offenders
questions.explanation: Traffic regulations govern road use for safety. Crashes are caused by speeding, drunk driving, bad roads, poor maintenance, distraction and overloading. The FRSC prevents crashes, rescues victims, educates road users and handles licences and number plates.

questions.stem:
(a) What is inter-personal relationship? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four skills needed to maintain good inter-personal relationships. [8 marks]
(c) State two ways of resolving conflicts peacefully. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Inter-personal relationship is the association, interaction or connection between two or more people
2 marks: Effective communication
2 marks: Active listening
2 marks: Tolerance and respect for others
2 marks: Empathy, honesty or cooperation
2 marks: Dialogue or negotiation
2 marks: Mediation by a neutral third party, or compromise
questions.explanation: Inter-personal relationships are interactions among people. They are sustained through communication, listening, tolerance, empathy and honesty. Conflicts are resolved by dialogue, negotiation, mediation and compromise.

questions.stem:
(a) What is cultism? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four reasons why students join secret cults. [8 marks]
(c) Suggest two ways by which cultism can be eradicated in Nigerian schools. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Cultism is the activities of secret groups whose members are bound by oaths and hidden practices, often involving violence
2 marks: Peer pressure
2 marks: Desire for protection or power
2 marks: Poor parental upbringing and lack of guidance
2 marks: Quest for popularity, financial gain or revenge
2 marks: Expulsion and prosecution of cultists
2 marks: Enlightenment campaigns, counselling and provision of wholesome recreational activities
questions.explanation: Cultism is membership and activity of secret, often violent groups. Students join through peer pressure, desire for protection or power, poor upbringing and greed. It can be curbed by firm sanctions, enlightenment and counselling.

questions.stem:
(a) Define drug abuse. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four effects of drug abuse on the individual. [8 marks]
(c) State two functions of the National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA). [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Drug abuse is the use of drugs without a doctor's prescription or in a manner or amount that harms the user
2 marks: Mental illness or psychosis
2 marks: Addiction or dependence
2 marks: Damage to organs such as the liver, kidneys and brain
2 marks: Poor academic performance, crime or death
2 marks: Arresting and prosecuting drug traffickers
2 marks: Destroying illicit drug farms or enlightening the public on the dangers of drugs
questions.explanation: Drug abuse is misuse of drugs. It causes mental illness, addiction, organ damage, school failure, crime and death. The NDLEA arrests traffickers, destroys drug farms and educates the public.

questions.stem:
(a) What is human trafficking? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four causes of human trafficking in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) State two functions of NAPTIP. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Human trafficking is the recruitment, transportation or harbouring of persons by force, fraud or deception for the purpose of exploitation
2 marks: Poverty
2 marks: Unemployment
2 marks: Ignorance and illiteracy
2 marks: Greed, family pressure or weak law enforcement
2 marks: Investigating and prosecuting traffickers
2 marks: Rescuing, counselling and rehabilitating victims, or public enlightenment
questions.explanation: Trafficking is exploiting persons moved by force or deceit. Causes include poverty, unemployment, ignorance, greed and weak enforcement. NAPTIP prosecutes traffickers and rescues and rehabilitates victims.

questions.stem:
(a) What is the meaning of HIV and AIDS? [4 marks]
(b) Explain three ways by which HIV is transmitted. [6 marks]
(c) State five ways of preventing the spread of HIV/AIDS. [5 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
2 marks: HIV: Human Immunodeficiency Virus, the virus that weakens the immune system
2 marks: AIDS: Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndrome, the advanced stage of HIV infection
2 marks: Unprotected sexual intercourse with an infected person
2 marks: Transfusion of infected blood or sharing unsterilised sharp objects
2 marks: From an infected mother to her child during pregnancy, delivery or breastfeeding
1 mark: Abstinence
1 mark: Faithfulness to one uninfected partner
1 mark: Screening of blood before transfusion
1 mark: Use of sterilised instruments
1 mark: HIV testing and antiretroviral treatment, including PMTCT
questions.explanation: HIV is the virus; AIDS is the syndrome at its advanced stage. Transmission is sexual, through blood and sharp objects, and mother to child. Prevention includes abstinence, faithfulness, safe blood, sterile instruments and testing and treatment.

questions.stem:
(a) What is youth empowerment? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four benefits of youth empowerment to the nation. [8 marks]
(c) Mention two government agencies that promote youth empowerment in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Youth empowerment is the process of equipping young people with skills, knowledge, resources and opportunities to become self-reliant and productive
2 marks: Reduction in unemployment
2 marks: Reduction in crime and youth restiveness
2 marks: Increase in national productivity and income
2 marks: Self-reliance and reduced dependence on government, or creation of future leaders
2 marks: National Directorate of Employment (NDE)
2 marks: SMEDAN, or NYSC (Skills Acquisition and Entrepreneurship Development programme), or Bank of Industry
questions.explanation: Youth empowerment equips young people to be self-reliant. It reduces unemployment and crime and raises productivity. Agencies include the NDE, SMEDAN and the NYSC skills programme.

questions.stem:
(a) Name the three arms of government. [3 marks]
(b) Explain two functions of each arm of government. [12 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
1 mark: Legislature
1 mark: Executive
1 mark: Judiciary
2 marks: Legislature: making laws
2 marks: Legislature: approving the budget or overseeing the executive
2 marks: Executive: implementing laws and policies
2 marks: Executive: maintaining law and order, or conducting foreign relations
2 marks: Judiciary: interpreting laws
2 marks: Judiciary: settling disputes or protecting fundamental rights
questions.explanation: The legislature makes laws and approves budgets; the executive implements laws and maintains order; the judiciary interprets laws, settles disputes and protects rights.

questions.topic: Democracy, Rule of Law and National Development
questions.stem:
(a) Define democracy. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four pillars of democracy. [8 marks]
(c) Explain two ways in which democracy promotes national development. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Democracy is government of the people, by the people and for the people, in which citizens rule directly or through elected representatives
2 marks: Rule of law
2 marks: Independent judiciary
2 marks: Free, fair and periodic elections
2 marks: Free press, or respect for fundamental rights, or multi-party system
2 marks: Accountability of leaders leads to better use of public resources
2 marks: Stability and respect for rights attract investment and encourage participation
questions.explanation: Democracy is rule by the people. Its pillars are rule of law, an independent judiciary, free elections and a free press. It promotes development through accountability, stability and investor confidence.

questions.stem:
(a) What is political apathy? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four causes of political apathy in Nigeria. [8 marks]
(c) Suggest two ways of reducing political apathy. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Political apathy is lack of interest or indifference of citizens towards political activities such as voting
2 marks: Electoral malpractice and rigging
2 marks: Political violence and thuggery
2 marks: Failure of leaders to fulfil campaign promises
2 marks: Poverty, illiteracy or ignorance of political rights
2 marks: Political education and voter enlightenment
2 marks: Conduct of free and fair elections and accountable leadership
questions.explanation: Apathy is indifference to politics. It results from rigging, violence, broken promises and poverty. It is reduced by voter education, credible elections and accountable leadership.

questions.stem:
(a) Explain the term civil society. [3 marks]
(b) Explain four roles of civil society organisations in a democracy. [8 marks]
(c) State two problems facing civil society organisations in Nigeria. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: Civil society refers to voluntary, non-governmental organisations through which citizens pursue common interests and influence public affairs
2 marks: Educating citizens on their rights and duties
2 marks: Monitoring elections
2 marks: Holding government accountable through advocacy and budget tracking
2 marks: Defending human rights or providing services to communities
2 marks: Inadequate funding
2 marks: Government hostility, internal division or partisanship
questions.explanation: Civil society comprises voluntary non-state organisations. They educate citizens, monitor elections, hold government to account and defend rights, but suffer from poor funding, hostility and division.

questions.stem:
(a) What is the public service? [3 marks]
(b) Explain four ways in which the public service contributes to a democracy. [8 marks]
(c) State two measures to reduce corruption in the public service. [4 marks]
questions.markingGuide:
3 marks: The public service comprises all persons employed by government in ministries, departments, agencies and parastatals to implement policies and deliver services
2 marks: Implementing government policies and programmes
2 marks: Advising political office holders on policy
2 marks: Providing continuity when governments change
2 marks: Delivering essential services to citizens, or keeping records and data
2 marks: Strict enforcement of the Code of Conduct and asset declaration
2 marks: Prosecution by EFCC/ICPC, or improved pay and use of the Freedom of Information Act
questions.explanation: The public service is government's permanent workforce. It implements policy, advises leaders, ensures continuity and delivers services. Corruption is reduced through asset declaration, prosecution, better pay and transparency.
